title: Database Connection Pool Exhaustion — Retail Banking API 503 Errors

content.summary: A slow query introduced in a new account-summary feature caused connection pool exhaustion on the retail-banking-api on 2024-07-25, resulting in HTTP 503 errors for 22,000 customers over 55 minutes.

timeline.event: retail-banking-api v5.2.0 deployed with new account-summary aggregation feature
p99 database query latency climbs from 80 ms to 4.2 s on /api/accounts/summary endpoint
Connection pool reaches 100 % utilisation; 503 errors begin
P2 declared; DBA team identifies missing index on account_transactions.account_id
Hotfix index created concurrently on live database
Query latency returns to 95 ms; connection pool drains; 503 errors cease

content.root_cause: The new account-summary aggregation query performed a full table scan on account_transactions (280 M rows) because the WHERE clause used a function on account_id that prevented index usage. The query was tested against a staging dataset of 50,000 rows which executed in < 100 ms, masking the production performance issue.
contributing_factors: Staging database not sized proportionally to production (0.02 % of production row count)
No query plan analysis required as part of feature review
Same connection pool exhaustion pattern as INC-2024-001 — recurring root cause

immediate: Feature flag: disable account-summary aggregation endpoint
short_term: Size staging database to minimum 10 % of production row counts (JIRA DB-450)
Add EXPLAIN ANALYZE gate to database-touching PRs (JIRA DB-451)
Fix query to avoid function on indexed column (JIRA RETAIL-890)
long_term: Introduce pre-production load testing for all new database queries against production-scale data
Add automated slow-query detection in CI using pg_stat_statements
Connection pool autoscaling with load-shedding circuit breaker
